hypotheses.justification: By `profileHistory_eq_initial_add_primitive`, `profileHistory P r p = profileInitial P r p.2 + ∫ x in 0..p.1, radialDensity r x (P.f (x,p.2)) (P.U (x,p.2))`. Here `primitive F p := ∫ x in (0:ℝ)..p.1, F (x, p.2)` and `profileDensity P r p = radialDensity r p.1 (P.f p) (P.U p)`, so the density at a point depends only on `f` and `U` at that same point. The initial terms agree, as in the given proof (`profileInitial_congr`). For the integral, use `intervalIntegral.integral_congr`. It only needs the integrands to agree on `uIcc 0 p.1`, whatever the sign of `p.1`. Every `x` in that set satisfies `x ≤ max 0 p.1`. This is `≤ radius N.endpoint δᵢ = N.endpoint * Real.exp δᵢ`: that radius is positive (`N.endpoint_pos`, `Real.exp_pos`), and `p.1 ≤ radius` by `hpᵢ`. So `refF_eq_natural` / `refU_eq_natural` (which need only `hη` and `x ≤ N.endpoint * Real.exp δ`) give `A.f = N.f = B.f` and `A.U = N.U = B.U` at `(x, p.2)`. When `p.1 < 0`, every such `x` is ≤ 0 < `N.endpoint`, and `refF_eq_natural_initial` already gives the same equalities. `hX` is only used to rewrite `uIcc 0 X` as `Icc 0 X` inside `profileHistory_congr_up_to`. Restating that congruence step with `uIcc`, or doing the integral congruence inline as above, removes the need for it. So the statement still holds and is provable without `hX`.
